prompt.es: Defiende tu postura sobre el caso nuevo y responde a dos objeciones.

answer.text: On balance, I would support starting school at half past nine, provided that the school day still finishes before five. It seems likely that students would be more awake in the morning, and they would probably learn more. Some people object that students will simply go to bed later. That is a fair objection; however, teachers could ask families to keep the same bedtime, and the school could measure the results for a few months. Others say the school day would end too late. I take your point, although it does not tackle the real problem: many students are tired at eight o'clock, and tired students learn little. A shorter lunch break would keep the day shorter. To sum up, I would support the change for a trial year, and I would review the evidence carefully before making it final.
accepted: On balance, I would support starting school at half past nine, provided that the school day still finishes before five. It seems likely that students would be more awake in the morning, and they would probably learn more. Some people object that students will simply go to bed later. That is a fair objection; however, teachers could ask families to keep the same bedtime, and the school could measure the results for a few months. Others say the school day would end too late. I take your point, although it does not tackle the real problem: many students are tired at eight o'clock, and tired students learn little. A shorter lunch break would keep the day shorter. To sum up, I would support the change for a trial year, and I would review the evidence carefully before making it final.

On balance, I am in favour of a later start, as long as lessons end at a reasonable time. It is likely that students would feel less tired and pay more attention. Some people say that students will go to bed later. I take your point, but parents could set a rule, and the school could check the results after a few months. Another objection is that the day would finish too late. That is a fair objection; however, a shorter break would help. To sum up, I would accept the change for one year and then review it.

feedback.es: La intervención necesita postura con condición, razón cautelosa, dos objeciones respondidas con tacto y un cierre.

origin.text: Caso nuevo: el colegio propone empezar las clases a las 9:30 en vez de a las 8:00. Prepara tu intervención (unas 130 palabras): defiende una postura matizada con una condición, da una razón con cautela, responde con tacto a dos objeciones («los estudiantes se acostarán más tarde» y «el día terminará demasiado tarde») y cierra con un resumen.

choices.text: I support the plan, always and without conditions.
The plan is perfect, end of discussion.
I would support the plan, provided that the cost stays low.

feedback.es: Would + provided that muestra apoyo con condición; las otras frases no admiten matices.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué condición pone la hablante.

choices.text: That classes do not end after five.
That students sleep longer at home.
That the school gets a new building.

feedback.es: Provided that we finish before five es la condición: que las clases no terminen después de las cinco.

origin.audio: On balance, I would accept the later start, provided that we finish before five. It seems likely that students would sleep better.

feedback.es: Fair objection reconoce que la objeción es razonable.
